outcome: No settlement of the Novikov conjecture is found since 26 January 2024; the main candidate is Tian and Yu (arXiv:2605.12930, first posted 13 May 2026, current version v8 of 25 Sep 2026), which claims the strong Novikov conjecture for every discrete group admitting a coarse embedding of finite complexity into the universal Banach space, while the other in-window results are restricted to classes of groups, analogues, or are conditional, and no expert engagement with the Tian–Yu claim was found.
problem_asks: (i) For every closed oriented manifold M with fundamental group pi, and every classifying map f: M -> B(pi) and every rational cohomology class x of B(pi), the higher signature <L(M) cup f*(x), [M]> (the statement's 'certain polynomials in the Pontryagin classes ... arising from the fundamental group') is invariant under orientation-preserving homotopy equivalence. (ii) The statement puts no restriction on pi, so the claim is for all groups pi and all such x. Parts (i) and (ii) together are the whole of what is asked. The equivalent form in the Wikipedia lead (rational injectivity of the L-theory assembly map) is the same claim in another guise; the statement itself does not require it, so no separate part is listed.

events.what_happened: Gong, Wu and Yu, 'The Novikov conjecture, the group of volume preserving diffeomorphisms and Hilbert-Hadamard spaces', arXiv:1811.02086, first posted 5 Nov 2018 (v4 1 Mar 2021, comment 'to be published in GAFA'). The abstract proves the Novikov conjecture for discrete groups admitting an isometric, metrically proper action on an admissible Hilbert-Hadamard space, presented as an infinite-dimensional analogue of Kasparov's theorem, with the corollary that geometrically discrete subgroups of the volume-preserving diffeomorphism group of a closed smooth manifold satisfy it.
events.revisions: v1 5 Nov 2018; v2 18 Jan 2019; v3 18 Sep 2019; v4 1 Mar 2021 (current). Journal publication in GAFA (2021) is reported by a search snippet (DOI 10.1007/s00039-021-00563-7); that journal page was not opened.
events.delivers: The Novikov conjecture for discrete groups with an isometric, metrically proper action on an admissible Hilbert-Hadamard space, and so for geometrically discrete subgroups of Diff_vol(M) of a closed smooth manifold M. Restricted to that class of groups.
events.remains: Every group outside that class, including general discrete groups.

checked_by.what_they_did: Publication in GAFA 2021 is reported by a search snippet; the referee process is not visible to me
checked_by.where: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.02086 (journal DOI from a search snippet, not opened)

events.direction: Proves the conjecture for the stated class, so it supports the conjecture within that class.

events.what_happened: Tian, Xie and Yu, 'Strong relative Novikov conjecture for coarsely embeddable groups', arXiv:2310.00379, first posted 30 Sep 2023. The abstract states a strong relative Novikov conjecture for any pair of groups that are coarsely embeddable into Hilbert space. The abstract does not state a consequence for the classical conjecture; a 2024 talk abstract (not opened) says it gives the classical conjecture for manifolds with boundary in that setting.
events.delivers: A relative version: the strong relative Novikov conjecture for pairs of groups both coarsely embeddable into Hilbert space. This is a changed question (a relative form for pairs), not the absolute conjecture for a single group.
events.remains: The absolute Novikov conjecture for a single group, and every group not coarsely embeddable into Hilbert space.
events.direction: Supports a relative analogue of the conjecture; does not settle the absolute statement.

events.what_happened: Gong, Wu, Xie and Yu, 'The Novikov conjecture, the group of diffeomorphisms and continuous fields of Hilbert-Hadamard spaces', arXiv:2310.01219, first posted 2 Oct 2023. The abstract says it proves the Novikov conjecture for discrete subgroups of the diffeomorphism group of a compact smooth manifold, removing the volume-preserving condition of the 2018 Gong–Wu–Yu work, by operator K-theory and group actions on continuous fields of infinite-dimensional non-positively curved spaces. A 2023 seminar abstract (not opened) describes the result as the rational strong Novikov conjecture for geometrically discrete countable subgroups.
events.revisions: v1 2 Oct 2023; v2 27 Aug 2024; v3 21 Feb 2025 (current). The arXiv page shows no journal reference.
events.delivers: The Novikov conjecture (abstract wording; the seminar wording is the rational strong form) for discrete subgroups of Diff(M) of a compact smooth manifold M. A restricted class of groups, and the volume-preserving restriction is dropped.
events.remains: Every group that is not a discrete subgroup of such a diffeomorphism group.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture within the stated class.

events.what_happened: Hervé Oyono-Oyono and Guoliang Yu, 'Quantitative index, Novikov conjecture and coarse decomposability', arXiv:2412.01314, posted 2 Dec 2024 (single version). The abstract defines quantitative assembly-map estimates for families of finite metric spaces, relates them to the Novikov conjecture, and says 'we provide a geometric proof of Novikov conjecture for groups with finite decomposition complexity'.
events.delivers: The Novikov conjecture for groups of finite decomposition complexity. The abstract does not say whether the strong, rational or integral form is meant. The class is confined to groups of finite decomposition complexity, which the abstract does not define.
events.remains: Groups without finite decomposition complexity, i.e. the general case.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for a class of groups; the abstract makes no claim beyond it.

events.what_happened: Liang Guo, Qin Wang, Jianchao Wu and Guoliang Yu, 'Hilbert-Hadamard spaces and the equivariant coarse Novikov conjecture', arXiv:2411.18538, posted 27 Nov 2024. For a bounded-geometry space X with a proper isometric action of a countable discrete group Γ that equivariantly coarsely embeds into an admissible Hilbert-Hadamard space, the abstract proves the rational equivariant coarse strong Novikov conjecture when Γ is torsion-free. For general Γ it introduces a rational analytic equivariant coarse Novikov conjecture and proves it under the same embedding hypothesis.
events.delivers: An equivariant coarse analogue of the strong Novikov conjecture for proper Γ-spaces X, in rational form, under an equivariant coarse embedding hypothesis. The abstract is about the Γ-space X, not the homotopy invariance of higher signatures of manifolds with fundamental group Γ.
events.remains: The Novikov conjecture for the group itself is not addressed by the abstract.
events.direction: Analogue only (coarse, equivariant). It is recorded because it is an in-window result on the strong Novikov family, but it answers a different question.

events.what_happened: Jinmin Wang, 'Non-negative scalar curvature on spin surgeries and Novikov conjecture', arXiv:2512.16535, posted 18 Dec 2025 (single version). For a closed aspherical manifold M, assuming the rational strong Novikov conjecture for pi_1(M), the abstract shows that on spin surgeries along regions with trivial induced map on pi_1, every complete metric of non-negative scalar curvature is Ricci-flat.
events.delivers: A scalar-curvature rigidity conclusion, conditional on the rational strong Novikov conjecture for pi_1(M). It does not establish the conjecture for any group.
events.remains: All of the problem. The paper assumes the case it would need.
events.direction: Uses the conjecture as a hypothesis; it does not bear on whether the conjecture holds, so it is recorded as a conditional result that a later pass should discount.

events.what_happened: Yuetong Luo, 'Codimension 2 transfer of signatures in L theory', arXiv:2510.22624, posted 26 Oct 2025 (v2 6 Nov 2025, whose comment reads 'a misunderstanding about the authorship in the first version'). The arXiv page lists a single author; a search snippet had named Luo and Schick. The abstract answers a question of Higson, Xie and Schick by giving the L-theoretic counterpart of their codimension-2 invariance theorem for the K-theoretic signature under unspecified homotopy conditions, and constructs a transfer map between the symmetric L-groups of pi_1(M) and pi_1(N) carrying the signature of M to that of N up to torsion of order at most 4.
events.delivers: A codimension-2 submanifold transfer result for L-theoretic signatures, up to torsion of order at most 4, under unstated homotopy hypotheses. The abstract does not mention the Novikov conjecture or higher signatures of closed manifolds.
events.remains: Homotopy invariance of higher signatures of closed manifolds in general. The abstract claims no Novikov case.
events.doubts: The abstract does not state the homotopy conditions, so I cannot tell whether the result touches homotopy invariance of higher signatures at all. Recorded as a neighbouring question; a later pass should check the full text before counting it.
events.direction: Concerns codimension-2 transfer of signatures, a different question from homotopy invariance of higher signatures for closed manifolds, unless the full text shows otherwise.

events.what_happened: Jianguo Zhang, 'The Baum-Connes and the Mishchenko-Kasparov assembly maps for group extensions', arXiv:2601.09615, posted 14 Jan 2026 (v2 29 Jun 2026, comment 'Minor modifications'). The abstract claims that the strong Novikov conjecture, the surjective assembly conjecture and the Baum-Connes conjecture with coefficients are closed under direct products, central extensions and extensions by finite groups; that the rational analytic Novikov conjecture with coefficients is preserved under extensions by finite groups; and that the paper gives 'new examples for the rational analytic and the strong Novikov conjecture beyond the class of coarsely embeddable groups'. The abstract does not name the new examples.
events.delivers: Closure of the strong Novikov conjecture under direct products, central extensions and extensions by finite groups, given the stated hypotheses on the normal subgroup and quotient, and unnamed new examples beyond coarsely embeddable groups. The gain is confined to groups obtained by these operations and to examples the abstract does not identify.
events.remains: Groups not built from known classes by these operations, and the general case. How far the unnamed new examples reach is not stated in the abstract.
events.doubts: The claims are abstract-level only; the new examples are not named, and the semi-direct product results rest on three stated partial conjectures along N. I did not read the full text.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture for groups built by the stated operations and for unnamed examples.

events.what_happened: Geng Tian and Guoliang Yu, arXiv:2605.12930, first posted 13 May 2026 as 'Embedding complexity into Banach spaces and the strong Novikov conjecture' (comment 'Comments Welcome'); the current version v8 (25 Sep 2026) is titled 'Embedding complexity into the universal Banach space and the strong Novikov conjecture'. The v1 and current abstracts (both read on arXiv abstract pages) state that every discrete group admits a proper affine isometric action on the universal Banach space (the l^2-sum of the spaces l^{2p}(N)), following Brown–Guentner and Haagerup–Przybyszewska, hence a coarse embedding into it; and the paper proves that the strong Novikov conjecture holds for any discrete group admitting a coarse embedding of finite complexity into this space. The abstract also argues that the non-sofic groups of Kun and Thom have Property A and therefore satisfy the Novikov conjecture. A search snippet of the paper's introduction (not the full text) says the paper answers Pestov's question in the negative and describes the main conclusion as rational injectivity of the higher index map, i.e. the rational strong form.
events.revisions: v1 13 May 2026; v2 7 Jul 2026; v3 19 Jul 2026; v4 23 Jul 2026; v5 13 Aug 2026; v6 20 Aug 2026; v7 15 Sep 2026; v8 25 Sep 2026 (current). The title changed between v1 and v8. I did not compare the texts of the versions.
events.delivers: The strong Novikov conjecture (abstract wording) for every discrete group admitting a coarse embedding of finite complexity into the universal Banach space. The full text was unreadable to me (the PDF returned compressed binary and the HTML version returned 404), so the definition of 'finite complexity' and the precise hypotheses are unverified. A search snippet describes the conclusion as the rational form; I could not resolve this against the abstract's unqualified 'strong'. Separately, if the Kun–Thom non-sofic groups have Property A, the paper says they satisfy the Novikov conjecture.
events.remains: Every countable discrete group that has no finite-complexity coarse embedding into the universal Banach space. Whether this set is empty is the decisive point, and I could not check it. Every countable group has a coarse embedding into the universal Banach space (Brown–Guentner; Haagerup–Przybyszewska, both cited in the abstract), so the question reduces to whether the finite-complexity condition holds automatically for all countable groups.
events.doubts: No error, erratum or critique was found. Points for the judging pass: (1) I did not read the full text, so the main theorem's hypotheses, the strong versus rational form and the definition of finite complexity are all unverified; (2) the Property A corollary for the Kun–Thom groups depends on those groups, whose construction is announced in OpenAI's Astra result of August 2026, which has not been peer reviewed and whose attribution is disputed (see disputes); the main theorem's abstract does not appear to depend on that corollary; (3) no expert engagement found in about five months; (4) the title changed between v1 and v8, so the scope may have changed, and I did not compare the versions.
events.direction: Claims to prove the conjecture for a class of groups. If finite complexity holds for every countable group, the abstract would settle the conjecture for all groups; the abstract does not say whether that is so. Which way it cuts for the problem as stated therefore depends on a fact I could not check.

events.what_happened: OpenAI announced on 1 Aug 2026 that an internal version of its forthcoming Astra model had produced ten results in mathematics and theoretical computer science. Among them, per secondary coverage, is an explicit non-sofic group, described by Fournier-Facio's preprint as 'the unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra' when quoting the OpenAI announcement. The others include a disproof of Connes's rigidity conjecture, Ehrhart's volume conjecture, and Erdős problems. The Rényi Institute news page calls the non-sofic proof 'AI-generated' and names Gábor Kun and Andreas Thom's earlier results as 'the two principal inputs'. OpenAI's own post and its GitHub repository were not reached; the description comes from SiliconANGLE (2 Aug 2026), the Rényi page, and search snippets.
events.revisions: Per secondary reports (not opened), OpenAI later updated its writeup to credit Thom and Kun.
events.delivers: The existence of a non-sofic group, which answers Gromov's 1999 soficity question as coverage describes it. This is a different problem from the Novikov conjecture. The only link to Novikov is the Property A corollary claimed by Tian and Yu (event tian-yu-2026), which applies to the Kun–Thom groups and not to the Astra announcement itself.
events.remains: The Novikov conjecture. The announcement does not discuss it; the SiliconANGLE summary of the ten results does not mention higher signatures or Novikov.

machine_checked.note: A 'sorry' count of zero is reported by SiliconANGLE. The OpenAI repository was not opened, and a Lean certificate shows the code compiles, not that the formal statements match the open problems.

events.doubts: No peer review as of the reports I read. Attribution is disputed: Andreas Thom says a key step traces to his 2019 work with Kun and that months of his ChatGPT conversations shaped it, and OpenAI researchers deny this (see disputes). Some critics describe the release as oversold (secondary report). A human audit preprint, arXiv:2608.14673, exists but I did not open it.
events.direction: Asserts the existence of non-sofic groups, cutting against the conjecture that all countable groups are sofic. Not a bearing on the Novikov conjecture.
events.object: A non-sofic group, reported as the unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra (per Fournier-Facio quoting OpenAI). The construction is explicit, and its proof is in OpenAI's 249-page collection, which I did not read. Not a non-constructive existence proof, per coverage.
people: Andreas Thom (credited input; disputes the attribution)

ai.disclosed_cost: Reported at roughly 2,000 dollars at 'Sol API rates' by a secondary aggregator (not verified).

events.what_happened: Francesco Fournier-Facio, 'A torsion-free non-sofic group', arXiv:2608.02025, posted 3 Aug 2026 (v2 14 Aug 2026, 'small changes after several comments on the first version'). The abstract says OpenAI announced a non-sofic group, the unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra, and that the paper exhibits a different source of examples, including torsion-free groups, using the same technical criterion. A secondary summary says the paper's Theorem 1.3 gives a finitely presented torsion-free non-sofic group (not checked against the full text).
events.delivers: Non-sofic groups, including torsion-free examples. It concerns soficity, not the Novikov conjecture, and the abstract does not discuss Property A.
events.remains: The Novikov conjecture is not addressed.
events.direction: Concerns soficity, a different question. Recorded as a neighbouring result.
events.object: A torsion-free non-sofic group, from a source of examples 'relying on the same technical criterion' as the OpenAI construction. Per the secondary summary, finitely presented (not checked against the full text).

events.what_happened: Alexander Engel, 'Banach strong Novikov conjecture for polynomially contractible groups', arXiv:1702.02269, first posted 8 Feb 2017 (originally titled 'Strong Novikov conjecture for polynomially contractible groups'). Per a search snippet of the abstract (not opened), it proves the Banach-category strong Novikov conjecture for groups of type F_{d+1} that are polynomially contractible up to order d, with exponent p = (d+2)/(d+1), and says the class includes automatic groups. Published as Advances in Mathematics 330 (2018) per a search snippet.
events.revisions: v1 8 Feb 2017 (title 'Strong Novikov conjecture for polynomially contractible groups'); v2 8 Mar 2017; v3 10 Apr 2018 ('Banach strong Novikov ...').
events.delivers: A Banach-category version of the strong Novikov conjecture for a class of groups (polynomially contractible, type F_{d+1}; includes automatic groups per snippet). A changed form (Banach rather than C*-algebraic), so it is recorded as an analogue.
events.remains: The Novikov conjecture for groups outside that class, and in the original (C*-algebraic) form for those groups as far as this paper is concerned.

disputes.summary: Andreas Thom says a key step in the Astra non-sofic group result traces to his 2019 paper with Gábor Kun, and that months of his ChatGPT conversations on related problems shaped it. OpenAI's Mark Sellke replied 'Regarding your conversations with ChatGPT: that did not happen'; Sébastien Bubeck told Wired 'We did not use their prompt or proofs to prompt our models'. Thom says the reply does not address whether his conversations were used in training. OpenAI reportedly later credited Thom and Kun in its writeup. This dispute concerns the non-sofic result, not the Novikov conjecture, but the Tian–Yu Property A corollary uses the Kun–Thom groups. Sources are secondary (news and aggregator reports, Thom's posts not opened).

summary: Sources: the Wikipedia article (opened; its lead, last edited 22 July 2026, still says the conjecture is proved for finitely generated abelian groups, that it is not known for all groups, and that no counterexample is known, and it mentions no 2024–2026 results); arXiv abstract pages for each event listed above (all opened); the Rényi Institute news page and a SiliconANGLE report on the OpenAI Astra announcement (opened, both secondary); and about 44 search results. Within the window, the candidate that moves the problem most is Tian and Yu (arXiv:2605.12930). Its abstract states the strong Novikov conjecture for any discrete group with a coarse embedding of finite complexity into the universal Banach space. Every countable group has a coarse embedding into that space (cited in the abstract), so whether the paper settles the problem for all groups turns on whether finite complexity is automatic. I could not read the full text: the PDF returned compressed binary and the HTML version returned 404. The abstract's 'strong' wording and a search snippet's 'rational' wording also conflict and remain unresolved. The other in-window results are narrower: Oyono-Oyono and Yu (Dec 2024) for groups of finite decomposition complexity; Guo, Wang, Wu and Yu (Nov 2024) for an equivariant coarse analogue, which is not the group statement; Zhang (Jan 2026) for closure under extensions with unnamed examples; and Wang (Dec 2025), which assumes the conjecture. Luo (Oct 2025) concerns codimension-2 transfer and is not clearly about homotopy invariance. The 2023 Gong–Wu–Xie–Yu result (rational strong Novikov for discrete subgroups of Diff(M)) and the earlier Gong–Wu–Yu result (GAFA 2021) are recorded as predating the window. The AI-linked chain is indirect: OpenAI's Astra announcement (1 Aug 2026) gave the non-sofic groups that Tian and Yu use for a Property A corollary. Astra's announcement does not mention Novikov, and I found no system named for any Novikov event. Nothing I found shows an AI system contributing to the Novikov mathematics, and the Tian–Yu full text was not readable, so its acknowledgements could not be checked. Expert engagement: no public reading, verification or critique of the Tian–Yu paper was found in about five months, and no erratum or withdrawal was found. Dead ends: no Quanta or Terence Tao post on the conjecture was found; no Lean formalisation of the conjecture was found in the DeepMind formal-conjectures repository, which I searched but did not open; no AI-attributed Novikov proof was found in eight AI-targeted queries; the AI4Math survey arXiv:2608.24961 and the Bader–Sauer higher property (T) paper arXiv:2511.20192 surfaced but were not opened and are not about Novikov; the DFG project of Thomas Schick (2025) on higher signatures is a funding page, not a result.
competing_reading: Tian and Yu's abstract, if the finite-complexity hypothesis holds for all countable groups, would settle the conjecture as stated, since the statement puts no restriction on the group. The reading that Wikipedia still implies, that the result covers a large but proper class, is correct only if finite complexity can fail. A separate reading: the AI-linked corollary (Property A for the Kun–Thom groups) is AI-adjacent and could be counted by a later pass as AI-involved progress on this problem, although the Novikov theorem does not depend on it as far as the abstract shows, and the Astra construction it relies on has not been peer reviewed and is disputed.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv:2605.12930 (current version v8, and v1): the definition of finite complexity, whether every countable discrete group has a finite-complexity coarse embedding into the universal Banach space (if so, the result covers all groups), whether the theorem is the strong or the rational form, and the acknowledgements, read for any AI or software statement. (2) Expert reading of the Tian–Yu argument by people working in this area, and any erratum or comment. (3) Whether the Kun–Thom non-sofic groups used in the Property A corollary are the same as the Astra groups (the Fournier-Facio description suggests the unit group of the binary Leavitt algebra), and the authors' own account of how the Astra proofs were produced (OpenAI's post and repository, not reached). (4) Later arXiv papers citing 2605.12930 and still calling the Novikov conjecture open, or citing it as a resolution.

incomplete: (1) The full text of arXiv:2605.12930 was unreadable (PDF returned compressed binary, HTML returned 404), so its main theorem's hypotheses, the definition of 'finite complexity', whether every countable group satisfies it, the strong versus rational form, and its acknowledgements (AI statement) are all unverified; the none_found for that event is therefore a statement about what I could read, not a verified absence. (2) OpenAI's primary Astra announcement and its GitHub repository were not reached; the Astra description rests on SiliconANGLE, the Rényi page, and search snippets. The Kun–Thom preprint of 7 Aug 2026 mentioned in Fournier-Facio's paper was not identified. (3) The pre-2024 literature was not enumerated as events beyond the handful listed (Gong–Wu–Yu 2018, Engel 2017, Tian–Xie–Yu 2023, Gong–Wu–Xie–Yu 2023). Classical landmark results (Yu's 1998 finite asymptotic dimension theorem, Kasparov–Yu, Higson–Kasparov, Connes–Moscovici for hyperbolic groups, Skandalis–Tu–Yu, Ogle's ℓ¹ result, Deng–Tian–Xie–Yu 2021, Lafforgue) are background cited in search results and were not opened or recorded as events. (4) The publication status of the 2023 Gong–Wu–Xie–Yu paper is unknown (no journal reference found). (5) I did not compare versions of 2605.12930 (title changed from v1 to v8). (6) The Wikipedia article's revision history was not checked. (7) Search coverage is that of a general web search engine, not arXiv's own listings, so a 2026 preprint may exist that these searches did not surface.

event.what_happened: Hervé Oyono-Oyono and Guoliang Yu, 'Quantitative index, Novikov conjecture and coarse decomposability', arXiv:2412.01314, posted 2 Dec 2024 (single version). The abstract defines quantitative assembly-map estimates for families of finite metric spaces, relates them to the Novikov conjecture, and says 'we provide a geometric proof of Novikov conjecture for groups with finite decomposition complexity'.
event.delivers: The Novikov conjecture for groups of finite decomposition complexity. The abstract does not say whether the strong, rational or integral form is meant. The class is confined to groups of finite decomposition complexity, which the abstract does not define.
event.remains: Groups without finite decomposition complexity, i.e. the general case.
event.direction: Supports the conjecture for a class of groups; the abstract makes no claim beyond it.

events.credibility_reason: Eight versions in about four months with a title change (scope may have shifted), no expert engagement found, and if finite complexity were automatic it would be an unremarked resolution of a landmark problem; the full text and the definition of finite complexity were never read. Established authors with a serious method and no identified error, so doubtful rather than set aside.
Unreviewed, attribution disputed, described only through secondary sources; in any case a different problem (soficity).

judgement.why: The statement asks for homotopy invariance of higher signatures for all groups. If the (rational) strong Novikov conjecture holds for a class of groups, the Novikov conjecture holds for that class. So the class-of-groups results (Gong–Wu–Yu, Gong–Wu–Xie–Yu, Oyono-Oyono–Yu, Zhang, Tian–Yu) are cases. Tian–Yu is the close call. The record cannot show that finite-complexity embeddings exist for every countable group, and Wikipedia and the absence of any reaction both point to a proper class, so I scored it as a case rather than whole. The relative, equivariant coarse, Banach and codimension-2 transfer results answer changed questions, so they are variants. Wang assumes the conjecture, so it is none. The Astra and Fournier-Facio non-sofic results concern a different problem, so they are variants. On AI: Astra's AI role belongs to soficity, not Novikov, and its systems[] is empty here. No Novikov event credits any AI system (F13). Gong–Wu–Xie–Yu (first posted October 2023) stays pre-snapshot because its revisions show no new mathematics.
judgement.doubts: Tian–Yu's full text was unreadable. If finite complexity holds for all countable groups, that event would be whole (claimed), and its acknowledgements were never checked for AI. Novikov for groups of finite decomposition complexity was probably known before Oyono-Oyono–Yu (their abstract calls theirs a 'geometric proof'), so it may be a new proof of a known case. The record does not establish this, so I scored it as a case. The GAFA and Advances journal acceptances rest on unopened search snippets.
